column1: # *** THE SEARCH FOR SANCHO LLERENA'S DEATH, 15 September 2026. ***
# The trees say 1832 and have never produced a document. His last certain trace is as a living witness in 1798.
# *** The control was run before the null was believed, and it passed. ***
*** SANCHO'S DEATH - SEARCHED, AND NOT FOUND, WITH A CONTROL THAT PASSED ***
column2: *** No indexed death or burial exists for Sancho Llerena in Uruguay under any spelling. *** A name search across Uruguay returns 401 loose results in which *** he appears only as father, father-of-bride, spouse or 'other' *** - never as the principal of a death. The two death-flagged hits are an S/v Lorena of Artigas, 1902, and a Castilla Llerena of Flores, 1924.
column4: *** THE CONTROL: are Montevideo church burials of that period indexed at all? *** A search for the surname Rodriguez, Montevideo, deaths 1828-1838, returns burials from *** 'Uruguay, Catholic Church Records, 1726-2000' at NUESTRA SENORA DEL CARMEN LA MAYOR, CORDON *** - dated 1832, 1833, 1838. *** That is the exact parish and the exact decade. *** Justa Pastora married at the Cordon in 1830, the 1831 godfather act is at the Cordon, and Dominga lived there. *** So burials of Sancho's own family's parish, in the years he is supposed to have died, ARE indexed - and he is not among them. ***

column2: *** No indexed death or burial for Maria Fernandez, wife of Sancho Llerena, in Uruguay, 1810-1870. *** The search returns her only in the records already held - as mother of the bride at Justa Pastora's marriage, and in the 1811 baptism of Luis Escolastico.
column4: *** THE SAME 1811 RECORD INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES HER PARENTS. *** FamilySearch's index gives her *** 'Parents Rosa Fernandez, Rodrigo Fernandez' *** - which is a third witness to what the 1811 baptism and the 1791 marriage act both say. *** Three sources, one couple, no disagreement. ***

column1: *** WHAT THE NULL DOES NOT MEAN, STATED BEFORE ANYONE ASSUMES IT ***
column2: *** The index is name-based, and an eighteenth-century surname mangled by a transcriber is invisible to it. *** And *** the Cordon is one parish of several *** - he could be buried at the Iglesia Matriz, at Canelones, or at Santa Lucia where his wife's family were vecinos.
column4: *** SO THE HONEST STATEMENT IS: HE IS NOT IN THE INDEX, NOT THAT HE IS NOT IN THE REGISTERS. *** *** The next step is to walk the Cordon burial register by image for 1826-1845 ***, which is a bounded job now that films are addressable by number, and to do the same for the Matriz. *** The trees' date of 1832 remains a tree. ***
